claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances. Let me start with:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 and still living at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18, there are specific conditions that need to be met. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** 

(For example, is he studying for A-levels, Scottish Highers, or similar qualifications at school or college?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! He's currently studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! 

Since Alex is 18 and studying for his A-levels, I need to confirm one more important detail:

**When did Alex turn 18, or when will he turn 19?** (I need to know the specific date if possible, or at least which month and year)

This is important because Child Benefit for young people in education can continue until a specific date related to their age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I need to provide you with Alex's age information. Could you clarify - are you asking when he turned 18, or do you need to know his exact date of birth? He's currently 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good question! Let me clarify what I need.

Since Alex is currently 18 and in full-time education (studying A-levels), Child Benefit can continue beyond age 16, but it stops on a specific date. The cut-off is the **31st August (or in some cases the date the course ends, if earlier) following their 19th birthday**.

So to determine if you're still eligible, I need to know:

**Has Alex already turned 19, or is he still 18?** If he's still 18, approximately when will he turn 19? (Just the month and year would be helpful)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's still 18 - he won't turn 19 until later this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful. Now I need to understand a bit more about his course:

**When is Alex's A-level course scheduled to end?** (For example, is he finishing this coming summer, or does his course continue beyond this year?)

This is important because Child Benefit stops on the earlier of either:
- 31st August following his 19th birthday, or
- The date his course ends

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His A-levels finish this summer - he'll be taking his final exams in May and June, so the course ends in June.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me also check a few more details to complete the assessment:

1. **Are you responsible for Alex?** (In other words, does he live with you, or do you contribute to the costs of looking after him?)

2. **Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes to both - Alex lives here at home with me, and yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you or Alex subject to immigration control, or do either of you have any restrictions on your right to reside in the UK?** (For example, certain visa conditions or immigration status that might restrict access to benefits)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we don't have any immigration restrictions - we have full right to reside here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just one final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's the summary:

✅ **Alex qualifies** because:
- He is 18 years old and in full-time non-advanced education (studying A-levels)
- His course ends in June this year, which is before he turns 19
- You are responsible for him (he lives at home with you)
- You both live in the UK with full right to reside
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for him

**Important note:** Your Child Benefit for Alex will continue until his A-level course ends in June. After that, Child Benefit will stop, even though he won't turn 19 until later in the year, because the benefit ends on whichever comes first - either the course ending or 31st August following the 19th birthday.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you're already receiving it, it should continue automatically until June when his course finishes.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
